problem: The tier-A way-out leaves out the source's first, controlled option: lowering the bar onto the safeties. It sends a beginner straight to dumping the bar backward. A beginner who reads it literally will throw the bar off at any failed rep, even when the safeties would let them sit it down.
evidence: c13 quote (rep-fail): 'Ensure your safeties or pins are set just below your lowest squat depth. This allows you to lower the bar onto the safeties if you can't complete the lift.' The re-fetched REP page lists '- Set the Safety Bars: ... lower the bar onto the safeties if you can't complete the lift. - Drop the Bar: If you must bail, push the bar backward...'. The wayOut text has only 'To bail, push the bar backward off your shoulders while you move your body forward'.
fix: Order the line as the source does. Example: 'Can't stand up? Lower the bar onto the safeties. If you must bail, push it backward off your shoulders as you move forward. Practise with light weight first.' (c13, c15).

problem: plate.end holds Yessis's '30-45 degrees from the vertical' as part of the end pose. problem: Open question 1. The two lines do not conflict, because they cover different situations. BarBend (c6) covers the normal end-of-set set-down from a seated press: catch the dumbbells on the knees or hand one to a spotter, and don't throw them from shoulder height. Fitness Volt (c5) covers a failed rep on the bench press: drop the weights out to the side. The bench variant therefore has a sourced fail-a-rep way out that the card leaves unused ('not used in any field'), and the tier-A bench sheets show none.
evidence: Re-fetched Fitness Volt: 'if you are unable to complete a rep of barbell bench presses, you could find yourself pinned ... This is less of an issue with dumbbells because, if you get stuck, you can simply drop the weights out to the side.' BarBend: 'considering how you'll get them down at the end of the set ... bring your knees up one at a time to catch the dumbbells ... There's no reason to chuck them from shoulder height onto the floor.' GGR: 'reverse the process and come off the bench with the weights'.
fix: Shown lines. Bench finish: keep c4 ('After the last rep, keep your arms bent and sit up; the dumbbells come back to your thighs'). Bench fail: add a step from c5, e.g. 'Stuck on a rep? Drop the dumbbells out to your sides.' (WEAK, one coach source; add 'away from your face' only if a source says it). Seated finish: 'Bring your knees up one at a time to catch the dumbbells, or hand one to a spotter. Don't throw them down from shoulder height.' (c6). Rewrite c5's text, which should no longer say 'conflict'.
